title: The pledge of Ridwan
hookLine: Uthman goes into Mecca as envoy and won't circle the Ka'bah without the Prophet; a rumor says he's been killed, and they pledge under a tree, Salamah three times (48:18; Bukhari; Muslim)

cards: Someone has to go into Mecca and talk. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Umar says the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sent Uthman ibn Affan, because no one was held in higher regard in Mecca than he was.
So Uthman goes in alone, to explain that they've come as pilgrims, not to fight. Then he doesn't come back. Time passes, and a rumor runs through the camp at Hudaybiyyah: Uthman has been killed.

teach.h: UTHMAN WON'T CIRCLE THE KA'BAH ALONE.
teach.b: First, a small detail about Uthman, from the early biographers. In Mecca, the Meccans told him: you're here, so go around the Ka'bah if you want to. He refused.

He would not circle it until the Messenger of Allah did. The thing they had all walked so far for was in front of him, and he wouldn't take it alone. Back at the camp, the Prophet called the people to pledge.

teach.h: HANDS IN HIS HAND, UNDER A TREE.
teach.b: He sat beneath a tree, and they came, one by one, and put their hand in his.
Salamah ibn al-Akwa, in Sahih Muslim, tells his own part. He pledged among the first. Later, in the middle of the crowd, the Prophet said: pledge, Salamah.
I already did. And again. So he pledged a second time.
Near the end, once more: Salamah, won't you pledge? I pledged at the start and in the middle. And again.
So he pledged a third time. The sources word the promise differently: Salamah says they pledged unto death; Jabir, also in Muslim, says they pledged not to flee.
And for Uthman, who wasn't there, the Prophet held up his right hand, said this is Uthman's hand, and pledged for him. Surah al-Fath gives the moment two verses.

teach.h: THE HAND OF ALLAH IS ABOVE THEIR HANDS.
teach.b: One says that those who pledge to the Prophet pledge to Allah, and then, in Pickthall's words: "The Hand of Allah is above their hands."
The other says Allah was well pleased with the believers when they pledged beneath the tree. From that verse the pledge takes its name: ridwan, good pleasure. Uthman turned out to be alive.
But the pledge had already been made, and made again.

how: Muslims honor the companions of the tree named in 48:18, and the pledge of Ridwan is taught as part of the story of Hudaybiyyah in sirah classes and in commentaries on Surah al-Fath.

o: a vow of silence taken before a long journey
the name of the tree where the pledge was made
good pleasure: Allah pleased with those who pledged

games.q: The pledge of Ridwan — tap the pairs.
p: the Prophet pledging for the absent
pleasure: Allah was pleased with them

s: Uthman circled the Ka'bah while he was in Mecca
the biographers say he refused to go around it before the Messenger of Allah did.
Salamah was asked to pledge again after he'd already pledged
in Muslim, the Prophet said 'and again', and he pledged at the start, the middle and the end.
the sources all word the promise the same way
Salamah says unto death; Jabir says not to flee.

games.q: you're Uthman, alone in Mecca as envoy. the Meccans say: you're here, go around the Ka'bah if you like. what do you do?
o: go around it; you've come all this way.
refuse until the Prophet ﷺ can.
go around it quietly, and tell no one.
games.why: the biographers say he refused: he would not circle it until the Messenger of Allah did.

practice: Bring to mind a promise you made once and haven't said out loud in a long time, to a spouse, a friend, a child, your own health, your faith if you have one.
Now, somewhere in the middle, make it again, quietly, in your own words, the way Salamah did when he was told: and again. If you pray, you can renew it before Allah.

wordCard.voice: Ridwan, good pleasure: the name of the pledge made beneath a tree at Hudaybiyyah, from surah 48:18, Allah was pleased with them. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: good pleasure, approval; the pledge is named after Allah being pleased with the believers in 48:18.

carryVoice: Your line: under the tree. A promise can be made more than once. See you tomorrow.
